context:
Goal: the owner-ruled phone-screen changes (Orphaned composer margin, the held word, Hand end-of-day) merge.
Problem (rule): the Pro-phone screen test shards (label pro-ui) show no green run on any pull request in the last 80 runs, the same 9 tests fail every time, and the merge tool refuses a red run, so no pull request with that label can merge.
Based on (measured): runs 45025120326, 45025191429, 45025121981, 45025202524 and 44981596640 all fail the same 9 tests; a one-word change to the Hand box title (PR 388) fails the same set.
Based on (read): debt tally-audit-contrast-flags calls three of these audits intermittent; main has no baseline run because the Duo shards do not run on main.
Departs from: main merges a native pull request only on a green run — option a lets one merge with a known failing set, option c skips one pull request's Pro shards.
Waiting on: your answer; the coordinator keeps the native pull requests parked and the other lanes run.

options.how: A debt records the 9 tests; a native PR merges when its own tests pass and its failing set stays inside them.
options.label: File the 9 tests as a known red and let native PRs merge inside that set
options.lose: The merge tool's rule must change, a real regression inside the 9 tests can hide, and this goes against your ruling that a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

options.how: A builder lane fixes or pins the audit and layout checks on the Tally and Packages screens; the iOS 27.2 simulator is suspected, unmeasured.
options.label: A lane fixes or pins the 9 tests first
options.lose: Native work stays unmerged for a time nobody can state yet.

options.how: The coordinator removes the label from PR 388 so only the Duo shards must pass.
options.label: Drop the Pro label on the Hand word PR 388 only
options.lose: It skips the Pro proof the label exists for, and goes against your own labelling rule.

short: Pro-phone screen tests are always red: accept, fix first, or drop a label

title: The Pro-phone screen tests fail the same 9 tests on every run: how should native pull requests merge?
why: Fixing the 9 tests first keeps a green run meaning something (coordinator's recommendation); a on one pull request at a time only if you say so.
